newsitem.title: USA: MCI brings Internet video broadcasts to millions.
newsitem.headline: MCI brings Internet video broadcasts to millions.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. and Progressive Networks Inc. said Tuesday they would offer a service to deliver audio and video programming to millions of daily listeners and viewers over the Internet.

The companies said the new service, known as "RealNetwork," will give a boost to the Internet as a mass broadcast medium by combining MCI's high-speed Internet backbone network -- one of the world's largest and fastest -- with Progressive Networks' multimedia streaming technology.
Streaming is a technology that enables large amounts of continuous audio or video programming to be transmitted over the Internet.

The companies said the service has the potential to reach 50,000 people at the same time and attract a daily audience of 10 million to 15 million through a combination of live and on-demand broadcasts via the Internet and private corporate networks known as intranets.
The RealNetwork also can be expanded to serve larger audiences as demand increases, said Rob Glaser, chief executive at Progressive Networks.

"That's just a start," Glaser said in a conference call with reporters and analysts. "We can see a clear path to doubling that number and doubling that again over time," he said of plans to make the technology capable of handling up to 200,000 simultaneous users in the future.
The largest number of simultaneous viewers of video programming on the Internet prior to the introduction of RealNetwork was 10,000 to 12,000, according to Glaser.

These are slim numbers compared with radio and television broadcast audiences that number in the millions -- a key reason why traditional media have hesitated to embrace the Internet as a broadcasting medium.

MCI and Progressive Networks are launching the RealNetwork as a service not only for broadcasters and content providers, but also for large corporations to transmit "live" and "on-demand" programming to large audiences.
On-demand refers to programming that computer users can request to be delivered at a scheduled time.

Among the big media companies planning to use the RealNetwork system are Walt Disney Co.'s ABC News; and ESPN, Disney's joint venture with Hearst Corp.; Home & Garden Television; Chicago-based JAMtv; and the Seattle Mariners baseball team.
ABC News has already added the RealNetwork multimedia capabilities to its ABCNews.com Internet site to broadcast live news feeds and on-demand reports from ABC News.

Atlantic Records plans to conduct live concerts in its virtual venue, Digital Arena, featuring its label artists. ESPN will use the RealNetwork to broadcast professional basketball games live on ESPN SportsZone, the companies said.

However, due to the slow transmission speeds of most home computer users' equipment, the basketball games will be carried as Internet radio shows, along with photos and game statistics, but without live-action video, company officials acknowledged.

Initially, the service will be targeted at corporations who might use the system on internal corporate networks to carry training programmes, company speeches or other events. Business users are more likely to have the high-speed Internet connections that make Internet video a realistic option.

MCI has made its Internet backbone broadcast-ready by placing Progressive Networks' splitter technology at strategic points throughout its Internet network, simplifying the process for Internet users to access RealNetwork broadcasts.
This integration greatly expands the number of people who can tune in to Internet broadcasts while introducing higher levels of audio and video quality over the Net.
MCI Communications is headquarted in Washington, D.C. Progressive Networks is based in Seattle, Wash. Microsoft Corp. holds a 10 percent stake in Progressive Networks.
